A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StreamSplat and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Content can be matched reliably across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, interpolation, runtime, and component-ablation results, including Tables 1–4 and appendix visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds zero-shot novel-view evaluations, Gaussian-persistence visualizations, and a runtime breakdown.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses, probabilistic sampling, and adaptive fusion are retained. Algorithm 1 revises the stated position update from mu0 + v*t to mu0 + v*(t-t0). Algorithm 2 additionally makes canonical-state updating and opacity pruning explicit; this expanded description does not establish a wholesale method replacement.

E1.justification: v2 adds zero-shot dynamic novel-view synthesis on seven DyCheck iPhone scenes and seven NVIDIA Dynamic Scenes (Appendix C, Tables 6–7). This substantially broadens evaluation beyond the retained RE10K, CO3Dv2, DAVIS, and YouTube-VOS coverage. Training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 newly evaluates a DGMarbles pipeline supplied with CUT3R-estimated intrinsics. The original RE10K, DAVIS, and interpolation comparator memberships are retained, including LDMVFI. The additional camera-information variants of 4DGS and DGMarbles do not constitute entirely new baseline families.

E3.justification: The added benchmarks introduce zero-shot protocols, DyCheck relative-camera evaluation trajectories, and controls using fixed, perturbed, or CUT3R-estimated intrinsics. NVIDIA comparisons also distinguish access to ground-truth poses and scene metadata. Existing training configurations, evaluation resolution, and RE10K view sampling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds Gaussian-identity persistence analyses (Figures 4 and 15), topology-change and occlusion cases (Figure 16), camera-intrinsic sensitivity comparisons, and a module-level runtime analysis. The original component ablations remain unchanged. Appendix D mentions a constant-opacity ablation, but its cited Figure 8 only shows the retained sampling and depth ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds per-scene results averaging 12.37 PSNR/0.69 LPIPS on DyCheck and 16.30/0.48 on NVIDIA Dynamic Scenes, alongside new comparator results and a 49 ms runtime breakdown (Tables 6–8). Original RE10K, DAVIS, interpolation, and ablation values are unchanged after matching relocated tables.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects temporal displacement to depend on t-t0, anchoring position at the Gaussian's creation time. The main-text depth mapping is also reconciled with the formula already present in v1's appendix. Projection, rendering, opacity, and loss mathematics otherwise remain unchanged; no new proofs or theorems appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction promote the existing adaptive fusion mechanism into a third named contribution and add an explicit 1200× speedup claim. The central claims of feed-forward, uncalibrated, online reconstruction of arbitrarily long streams remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix D substantially expands interpretations of orthographic projection, opacity deformation, bounded velocity, and reconstruction versus generation. Appendix E adds residual distortion under strong perspective effects as a limitation. Earlier pseudo-depth and limited-history limitations are retained, while the existing explanation of weaker static novel-view performance moves to Appendix C.

D1.justification: v2 adds spatial scaling factors, explicit online pseudocode, single-A100 runtime details, and DINOv2 licensing; the code/model pointer changes to the project website. Training and architecture tables remain unchanged. Conversely, simplified Algorithm 1 omits several explicit parameter activations and scaling operations documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including MoSca, Shape of Motion, STORM, CUT3R, and the new evaluation datasets, while removing several earlier references, including LDMVFI's citation despite retaining its results. Positioning emphasizes translating offline deformation and fusion principles into online reconstruction; the central research positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial method passages are rewritten. Dynamic evaluation precedes static evaluation; detailed decoding and static-comparison discussion move into appendices. Discussion and limitations become separate sections, and citation style and conference formatting change throughout.

P2.justification: v2 revises the teaser, adds a simplified framework diagram while retaining the detailed original in the appendix, and adds opacity, persistence, topology-change, and novel-view displays. The full RE10K table moves to Appendix C with a condensed main-text summary, and v1 Figure 7 is split across v2 Figures 7 and 11.

improvement.justification: The new dynamic novel-view evaluations, persistence visualizations, runtime breakdown, and perspective limitation make v2 more informative and better supported. These gains are tempered by differing camera information across comparisons, lost activation details, and evidence mismatches in Appendix D: the Windmill baseline is stated as 10.61 PSNR versus 10.32 in Table 6, and Figure 8 does not support the claimed opacity ablation. The net quality improvement is limited.
